editorial:
Ever wondered what actually goes into making a skate video? You get a front-row seat to that chaos here. You follow the Carhartt WIP team as they tear through different European cities, but it is not just a highlight reel of tricks. You get to see the riders in their normal lives, the friendships they share, and the funny, stressful moments that happen when a trick just won't land. It feels less like a polished movie and more like you are hanging out with a group of talented friends who are obsessed with their craft.

What really makes this work is how it shows the grind. You see the failures and the long hours, which makes the final successful clips feel way more rewarding. The pacing stays snappy, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you are only there for the big jumps. If you want the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the crisp detail of the city streets. Or, if you are a real collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing the final edited version of the footage the crew spent two years filming. You see the payoff of all those failed attempts and long trips across Europe. It ends with a montage of the team celebrating their hard work. There is no big plot twist since it is a documentary, but the conclusion leaves you feeling inspired by their dedication to skateboarding and their bond as a team.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves extreme sports and street culture.
